name: Tova Deepcoal
title: stonewright
why: At the foot of the Last Bridge, reading its stones. Word reached Cinderforge that somebody in Hearthvale had built a thing, and she walked up to see whose work it was.
examine: Tova Deepcoal is a Cinderfolk stonewright. She is forty, which is young for Cinderfolk.
She taps the bridge with a small hammer, listens, and writes nothing down.
Her great-great-grandfather was the Stonewright of the Old Company. She has not brought it up.
meet: Mind the third stone. It’s sound. I only say mind it because I’ve just been listening to it and it’s shy.
Tova Deepcoal. Stonewright. I heard somebody built something down the road. Was that you? It’s decent work.

wary: You again. The bridge is still up. I’d have told you.
neutral: Hello. I’m on the fourth stone today. It’s taking its time. So am I.
warm: Ah, the builder. Come and listen to this one. It’s got a good note in it.
fond: There you are. I’ve been keeping a stone for you. It’s only a small one. It rings.

tired: That’s my listening done for today. Stone takes it out of you. Come back tomorrow.
finished: I’ve said what I know. The rest is in the stones, and they talk slower than I do.

say: Every stonewright has a note. You tap a stone and it answers in your note. My family all have one. I’m forty and mine hasn’t turned up.

options.text: What does the tapping tell you?
reply: Where it’s tired. Where it’s proud. This one’s proud. It was laid by somebody patient.
For Cinderfolk it’s Tuesday morning. I know. I still check every stone.

options.text: Maybe your note is a rest.
reply: That’s a music joke. I’m a mason.
Everybody says so. They all had theirs by thirty.

say: A bridge is a promise between two sides. You raise one and both sides have to keep it up. Most people raise them and walk off.

options.text: How do you know when one’s failing?
reply: It goes quiet. A good bridge hums. I’d draw every one you’ve got and mark the quiet ones.

options.text: I’ve raised a few and walked off.
reply: I know. I walked up three of them to get here. Steady now. They’ll mend.
They’re weighted to my hand. You’d walk in a circle.

say: My great-great-grandfather built half of what’s standing. He sells tea now. People ask if I’m as good as him. I don’t know. He won’t look at my work.

reply: This. The cap on the fourth stone. I set it this morning. Nobody asked me to. Listen.

options.text: He might be afraid it’s better.
reply: I hadn’t thought of that. I don’t think I’ll think of it again. Thank you, though.
I’m somebody’s great-great-granddaughter with a hammer. It’s a start.

errand.title: A capstone
offer: The bridge wants one more cap. I’ve the mortar and the hammer. I haven’t the stone. I’ve tapped every one on this bank and they’re all busy.
Bring me four stone. Plain is fine. I’ll find the one that wants to be here.
waiting: No stone yet. That’s all right. The bridge has stood three hundred years. It can stand a week.
done: Four. This one. Hear that? No. Nor do I. But it sat down straight away, and that’s something.
Keep the offcut. It’s the first piece I’ve cut that I didn’t want to cut again.

keepsake.name: A stone offcut
keepsake.text: The first piece Tova cut that she didn’t want to cut again.

memories.asked-about-the-tapping: You asked what the tapping tells her. This bridge is proud, and was laid by somebody patient.
memories.asked-about-quiet-bridges: You asked how she knows a bridge is failing. It goes quiet. She offered to draw every one of yours.
memories.asked-to-see-her-work: You asked to see something she built. She showed you the cap on the fourth stone, set that morning.
memories.brought-the-capstone: You brought her four stone, and one of them sat down straight away.

early: A camp. I’d want to see how you build first. Not what. How. Ask me something about stone.
ask: Your camp. Is anything in it level? No. Don’t tell me. I’d rather find out.
I’d keep a ledger of your bridges. Every one drawn, and the quiet ones marked. I wouldn’t nag. The drawing nags.
yes: Then I’ll come. Steady now. I’ll need a flat place for the hammer and a wall to disapprove of.
full: No bed. I’ll sleep at the bridge. It’s been promised to both sides. That’s more than most beds.
camp.role: Draws every outside connection as a bridge, and marks the quiet ones.
camp.leaves: One stone by the fire that rings when tapped.

wants.now: A capstone for the Last Bridge.
wants.next: Something of her own to build, from the ground.
wants.really: To tap a stone and hear her own note come back.
wants.worry: That the note went to somebody else in the family.

favourites.food: black tea, strong enough to stand a chisel in
favourites.place: the underside of a good arch
favourites.topic: who laid a stone, and how
favourites.person: anyone who looks after what they built

aversions: bridges raised and walked away from
sheet.temperament: Steady, exacting and slow to say a kind thing she means.

voice.rhythm: Even, unhurried sentences. A judgement of the work, then a small allowance.
voice.hello: Says which stone she is on.
voice.goodbye: Says stone takes it out of you.

birch: Birch. It’d do for a wedge. Wood’s a short-term material. No offence to it.
ash: Ash. That’s a hammer handle. Mine’s sound. I’ll keep this for the day it isn’t.
pine: Pine. It moves when it’s wet. I don’t build with anything that has moods.
minnow: A fish. I don’t know what to tap. I’ll ask someone.
trout: A trout. Good weight to it. Well made. Whoever built it knew what they were doing.
berries: Berries. They stain mortar. I found that out at nine. I’ll eat them over here.
herbs: Herbs. For the tea. My great-great-grandfather would have views. He’s not here.
stone: Stone. Let me hear it. Good. That’s a willing stone. Decent work, bringing it.
copper: Copper. That’s a cramp for two stones that don’t get on. I know just the two.

day.morning: Morning. The stone’s cold and honest. Best time to listen.
day.afternoon: Afternoon. The sun’s on the south face. It rings a bit sharp. I allow for it.
day.evening: Evening. The bridge settles about now. You can hear it sit down.
day.night: I sleep against the abutment. It’s warm from the day. It doesn’t fidget.
day.rain: Rain. Good. You see where water wants to go. Then you build so it can.

wendell: The man in the road measured this bridge for me. End to end. He was a hand’s breadth out and told me so.
rivet: The sergeant oils hinges nobody asked him to. I set caps nobody asked for. We haven’t discussed it.
mags: The quartermaster mends seams. I mend joints. She uses a laser. I think that’s cheating. I want a go.

asked-about-the-tapping: I tapped the fifth stone after you left. Tired. I’ve given it the afternoon off.
asked-about-quiet-bridges: I’ve started the drawing. Three of yours hum. One’s gone quiet. I’ve marked it gently.
asked-to-see-her-work: The cap’s still sitting right. I check it when nobody’s on the bridge.
brought-the-capstone: That stone’s settled in. The ones either side have stopped complaining.

wary: You again. The cap’s on. You brought the stone. I don’t forget who brings stone.
neutral: Hello. The bridge is finished. It was finished before. Now it’s finished and I helped.
warm: Ah, the builder. The bridge is capped. I want something of my own next. From the footing up.
fond: There you are. One cap, sat straight. I’m drawing a thing of my own. Don’t look yet.

arc.complication: A family note that has not come to her.
arc.kindness: Someone asks to see what she built.
